request_note: issue body preserved verbatim, with images replaced by [image omitted]; all subsequent discussion removed
pre_change_note: Parent commit of PR #3049 squash merge commit df7415eb (#3065 also refers to dff251c2a1 as the pre-change version)
historical_wrong_note: HexElementLatent removes heaConVapCoi (latent heat no longer enters the coil metal node); water-side Q1 equals only sensible heat, leaving the latent heat portion unbalanced (issue #3065)
final_correct_note: PR #3073 merged: reverts the changes to HexElementLatent in df7415eb and changes the inlet air humidity in the validation model added by the PR from supersaturated to RH 99.5%; after the revert, approximately 17 W (≈1% of the design heat flow) of residual sensible heat remains with fully saturated inlet air; the author of #3065 considers this a modeling approximation, not a defect
invariant: Steady-state energy conservation for wet coils (WetCoilCounterFlow / WetCoilDiscretized / HexElementLatent): the sum of water-side heat gain Q1_flow and total air-side heat gain (sensible heat + latent heat) Q2_flow is 0, meaning that the coil neither creates nor destroys energy; the evaluation configuration is implemented using port enthalpy flows: m1*(h1_out-h1_in) + m2*(h2_out-h2_in) + (enthalpy flow carried away by condensate, per the library convention) = 0. Applies to SteadyState or constant inputs as t→∞
convention_note: Whether latent heat is accounted for at the coil surface or in the air volume is a modeling choice, but in either case, the total water-side and air-side heat flows must be equal and opposite at steady state; the statement in #3065 that “Q1 should be the negative of Q2” expresses this property

regression_examples.note: The energy imbalance in #3065 was discovered in this model
